info.title: Blockdaemon Wallet API
info.description: Wallet for storing, managing and transferring various coins and protocols

get.description: Retrieve a summary of all assets including the asset type, total balance and amount in USD.

parameters.name: exclude_empty
parameters.description: If set, exclude all entries which are empty

post.summary: Add an Additional Address to an Asset
post.description: Adds an address to the asset uniquely specified by VaultId and Asset. The name specified for the address must be unique. Be aware that this endpoint will not work for ethereum assets, since it is only possible to have a single address for such assets.

post.summary: Add Support for an Additional ERC20 Asset
post.description: Adds support for new ERC20 asset. Be aware that this endpoint will only work for ethereum based ERC20 assets. An Icon can be provided, however leaving it empty will give it either the Icon we have on file for the asset, or our default Icon.

get.summary: Get a List of Assets and Their Exchange Rate
get.description: Retrieves a list of all assets and their respective exchange rate. The list is in descending order based on the USDRate. If the asset does not have an exchange rate, USDRate will be set to null. If the asset has a pending exchange rate update the PendingUSDRate field will be set, if not it will be null

post.description: Given a failed address, this will attempt to generate the address again using the given parameters

post.summary: Set Exchange Rate of an Asset
post.description: Sets the exchange rate of asset specified by asset.The Rate should be set in USD. You can either set a fixed rate or set a range the rate is allowed to move in. If the range is set, the rate will be set by querying 3'rd parties and used so long they are in the given range. The exchange rate can only be set on assets with "Status" = "Success"

UserIds.description: The IDs of the users you wish to add.

ApprovalGroups.description: If present, the names of the groups which should approve of which we require at least one element in the list. Multiple elements are interpreted as OR. If not present it signifies All Users

NoOfApprovals.description: The number of approvals required for this expression to be true. The special value of -1 means all approvers in the given group/union of groups must approve

Name.description: The name of the group. Must be case-insensitively unique.

CreatedAt.description: When the notification was created in the wallet system

CreatedBy.description: Indicates the user which initiated the notification. In some cases, this can be 'System' as well

JsonSerializedDetails.description: Json serialized data which, when unpacked, reveals more details about the notification. The model depends on the notification topic

Seen.description: Indicates if the asking user has seen the notification before or not

Index.description: Determines the indices where this error occurred (only really useful for nested objects where multiples of the same structure appears). If we e.g. have an array with another array inside, we would need a level indicator of i.e. [1,0]. If the array is empty, as is most common, the error refers to the struct in the context

page.description: Page is the current page number

total.description: Total is the total number of results

customer_id.description: CustomerID is the unique identifier of a customer

title.description: Title is a human-readable plan title

total_active.description: TotalActive is the number of active validators

total_available.description: TotalAvailable is the number of available validators

total_pending.description: TotalPending is the number of pending validators

total_reserved.description: TotalReserved is the number of reserved validators

CorrelationId.description: CorrelationId is a convenience field since it's also declared as normal in the response header

Detail.description: Detail is a human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem. If present, it ought to focus on helping the client correct the problem, rather than giving debugging information

ErrorCode.description: ErrorCode denotes a fine-grained way of defining application specific errors

Errors.description: Errors is a list of validation errors which is present only if the Status is 400

Instance.description: Instance is a URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem.  It may or may not yield further information if dereferenced.

Status.description: Status is the HTTP status code ([RFC7231], Section 6) generated by the origin server for this occurrence of the problem.

Title.description: Title is a short, human-readable summary of the problem type. It SHOULD NOT change from occurrence to occurrence of the problem, except for purposes of localization (e.g., using proactive content negotiation; see [RFC7231], Section 3.4)

Type.description: Type is a URI reference [RFC3986] that identifies the problem type. This specification encourages that, when dereferenced, provides human-readable documentation for the problem type (e.g., using HTML [W3C.REC-html5-20141028]). When this member is not present, its value is assumed to be blank
